title: Playing funerals and taps at the grave
summary: Funerals across the river, marches on the way, lively playing and beer party after.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: There's one other question and we don't want to keep you very late. Then you're just about out of tape. Did you ever play any funerals? Oh, yes.
Yes. I played funerals. Most of our funerals were played over the river for these fire companies. These volunteer fire companies would have a band. We'd play most of them in Gretchen.
Did you play ragtime on the way back from the cemetery?

Yeah. We used to play marches, dearges we called them. Daaaahhhhhh. Monk Hays' daddy used to play bass drum with us. I liked Monk Hays' daddy how to play bass drum with the tub and the pop covers. That's easy to say.
Then after the funeral did you all...

Then after the funeral, coming back then he used to... Be glad you did your rascal, you know, all that kind of stuff. Coming back, then they'd have a big beer party at the firehouse, see? Coming back. And we have a wonderful time.
What did you have at the grave, what they did at the funeral? Once more and get it on the tape.
At the grave, one trumpet player stands back in the crowd and blows taps. When he gets through, another man falls off. Way back away, he blows taps like an echo. See? And then after that...
